preamble: Crossing solutions to the clues clash in eight of the squares. The correct letters to enter in the puzzle spell out, in grid order top to bottom, a name connected with the unclued solution to 17 16, which may help you solve these clashes, while still entering only real words.

clue.text: Were very hungry dean and reverend briefly out?

indicators.note: out means put out of order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
Rev is the short form of Reverend

explanation.surface: Were two clergymen starving, or simply not in?
explanation.walkthrough: Dean and Rev sound like two churchmen who have gone out; their letters are the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: To raven is to devour greedily, so to have ravened is to have been ravenous.

clue.text: Bird some metres to the north

indicators.note: in a down clue, going north means reading upwards, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: any and some both mean an unspecified amount
M is the SI symbol for metres

explanation.surface: A bird spotted a few metres further north.
explanation.definitionFit: The myna is a starling-like Asian bird famous for mimicking speech.

clue.text: Alcoholic drink and food includes self-catering

indicators.note: the meal holds the abbreviation inside it

parts.note: a meal is food eaten at one sitting
SC is the abbreviation used in holiday listings for self-catering

explanation.surface: A holiday deal with drinks and meals, though you cook for yourself.
explanation.definitionFit: Mescal is a Mexican spirit distilled from agave, a cousin of tequila.

clue.text: Novice in love, slowing up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: rit, short for ritardando, is the musical direction to slow down
love is zero in tennis, which looks like O

explanation.surface: Someone new to romance, taking things slowly.
explanation.walkthrough: The clash with 9 Across puts H in the second square, giving THRO, an old spelling of through, and the H of THE.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiro is a beginner or learner, from the Latin for a young recruit.

clue.text: Day small boy gets a thrill

parts.note: Fri is the short form of Friday
a son is a boy child

explanation.surface: A little lad has an exciting day.
explanation.definitionFit: A frisson is a sudden shiver of excitement or fear.

clue.text: Breakdown of relative after obsessive year

indicators.note: the relative comes after the obsessive year, so it goes at the end

parts.note: anal is the informal word for fussily obsessive about detail
sis is short for sister, a relative

explanation.surface: A family member's collapse following a year of fixation.
explanation.walkthrough: This is one of the eight clashing squares: the clue gives ANALYSIS, but the grid takes T from 8 Down, giving the real word ANALYSTS and the T of THE CLASH.
explanation.definitionFit: An analysis breaks a thing down into its parts for study.

clue.text: Developed the slogan for director's technique

indicators.note: developed means worked into a new form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A film-maker's method grew out of a catchphrase.
explanation.walkthrough: Developed suggests film being processed, which fits the director but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An angle shot is a camera shot taken from an unusual tilt, a device film directors use.

clue.text: Drink's temperature not quite chilled

indicators.note: not quite means the last letter is left off

parts.note: a drink on ice is chilled

explanation.surface: A drink served a little warmer than it should be.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonic water is a mixer, a fizzy soft drink flavoured with quinine.

clue.text: Foreign address in rocky northern shore

indicators.note: rocky means unsteady, so the letters are shaken into a new order

parts.note: N for northern, as on a map
taken as written

explanation.surface: A letter sent abroad to a house on a craggy coast up north.
explanation.walkthrough: Address here is a form of address, a title, not a place to send post.
explanation.definitionFit: Senhor is the Portuguese title for a man, the equivalent of Mr or sir.

clue.text: Faster runs in course

indicators.note: runs as in a run-of-colour dye, letting the letters move into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A quicker athlete runs in a race over a set course.
explanation.walkthrough: Course looks like a running track; it is a course of a meal. Afters is British slang for pudding.
explanation.definitionFit: Afters is the dessert course that follows the main meal.

clue.text: Impress with hot and good weather

parts.note: in and hot both mean fashionable
rain is one kind of weather

explanation.surface: Wowing people with a heatwave and fine conditions.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue gives INGRAIN; the clash with 1 Down puts E in the first square, giving the variant spelling ENGRAIN and the E of THE CLASH.
explanation.definitionFit: To ingrain an idea is to impress it deeply and permanently on the mind.

clue.text: Old impostors to put in entertaining places

indicators.note: the word to is put into the middle of the places

parts.note: fairs are places of entertainment with rides and stalls
taken as written

explanation.surface: A charge to plant con men of the past in places of amusement.
explanation.walkthrough: Faitor is an archaic word for a cheat. The grid takes C from 3 Down, giving FACTORS and the C of THE CLASH.
explanation.definitionFit: A faitor was a medieval word for a fraud or swindler, especially one feigning illness to beg.

clue.text: It helps you look and see my clue is wrong

indicators.note: the words are in the wrong order and need rearranging

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: The setter invites you to spot an error in this very clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Muscles around the eyeball turn it, which is how you direct your gaze.

clue.text: Payment from Maori in skirt but no top

indicators.note: with no top means the first letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: a tutu is a ballet dancer's skirt

explanation.surface: A Maori dancer is paid while wearing a skirt and nothing above.
explanation.definitionFit: Utu is the Maori concept of recompense or reciprocal payment, used in New Zealand English.

clue.text: Catch or miss nothing

parts.note: a miss is a young woman, a lass
O looks like zero

explanation.surface: A choice between holding the ball and dropping it.
explanation.walkthrough: Catch or miss reads as opposites in a game; or here is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: To lasso an animal is to catch it with a looped rope.

clue.text: See 17 across
See special instructions

parts.note: the clue gives no wordplay; the preamble says this unclued answer is linked to the name spelt by the clashing letters
the solver is sent to the preamble, whose clashing letters spell the band that recorded this song

explanation.walkthrough: Unclued: the eight clashing squares spell THE CLASH, and their best-known single, with 16 Down, completes the title. The clashes themselves illustrate the song's dilemma of which letter should stay or go.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1982 hit by the punk band the Clash asks the question of whether to stay or leave.

clue.text: Least interesting setter enters clad in antique fashion

indicators.note: the setter goes into the archaic word

parts.note: drest is an old spelling of dressed
the setter refers to themselves as I

explanation.surface: The dullest compiler turns up in period costume.
explanation.definitionFit: Dry writing or talk is dull, so the driest is the least interesting.

clue.text: Half-hearted girl's stories

indicators.note: half of the two letters at the heart of the name is lost

parts.note: Anna is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl tells her tales without enthusiasm.
explanation.definitionFit: Ana is a collection of anecdotes or sayings about a person, a crossword-friendly word.

clue.text: Shopkeeper almost bags new coins

indicators.note: bags means holds inside, so the new letter goes into the trader
almost means the last letter is left off

parts.note: a florist keeps a flower shop

explanation.surface: A trader nearly pockets some freshly minted money.
explanation.definitionFit: A florin was a British coin worth two shillings before decimalisation.

clue.text: Troops tucked into rum, time for scrap!

indicators.note: the troops are tucked inside the strange word and the time that follows it

parts.note: rum is old British slang for odd or strange
men are soldiers, troops

explanation.surface: Soldiers drink rum before the time comes to fight.
explanation.walkthrough: Rum is not the drink, and scrap is not a fight: it is a leftover piece.
explanation.definitionFit: An oddment is a leftover fragment or remnant.

clue.text: Mythical maiden rested, returning her letters?

parts.note: Io was a maiden loved by Zeus in Greek myth

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: sat is to have rested on a seat

explanation.surface: A legendary girl had a lie-down, then wrote back to her letters.
explanation.walkthrough: Her letters suggests correspondence; the question mark flags that Io, being Greek, owns iotas. The clash with 20 Down puts L first, giving LOTAS, brass water pots, and the L of CLASH.
explanation.definitionFit: An iota is a Greek letter, so Io's name contains her own letters.

clue.text: Lose it on interrupting court favourite

indicators.note: the little word breaks into the middle of the favourite

parts.note: in tennis a seed is a player ranked to go far
re means on, concerning

explanation.surface: A top tennis player throws a tantrum on court.
explanation.definitionFit: To see red is to lose your temper, an idiom from the bullfighter's cape.

clue.text: Introduced one cultivated, welcoming two Poles

indicators.note: welcoming means taking in a guest, so the poles go inside

parts.note: land is cultivated by being tilled
N and S are the north and south poles

explanation.surface: A farmer brought in from abroad welcomes a pair of Polish workers.
explanation.walkthrough: Poles look like people from Poland. The clash with 19 Down puts A in the fifth square, giving INSTALLED and the A of CLASH.
explanation.definitionFit: To instil a feeling is to introduce it gradually into someone's mind.

clue.text: Not all accepting head of music department

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so the letter goes inside

parts.note: some is part but not all

indicators.note: head of means the first letter of the word

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Not everyone welcomes the new head of the music department.
explanation.walkthrough: Department is not a school division but a French administrative region.
explanation.definitionFit: The Somme is a département of northern France, named after its river.

clue.text: Soldiers performing rites for old cavalrymen

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps

indicators.note: performing means acting out, so the letters are put through a new routine

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Troops carry out ceremonies for veterans of the horse regiments.
explanation.walkthrough: The clash with 27 Down puts S third, giving RESTERS and the S of CLASH.
explanation.definitionFit: Reiters were German mounted soldiers of the 16th and 17th centuries.

clue.text: Special police force turned over kind of cell

indicators.note: turned over means flipped, so the letters read from the bottom up

parts.note: the Met is London's Metropolitan Police

explanation.surface: A special police unit raids a prison cell.
explanation.walkthrough: Cell suggests a jail; here it is the biology sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A stem cell is an unspecialised cell that can develop into other types.

clue.text: Amateur about to speak ill of millions in religious movement

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a ham is an amateur, as in ham radio or ham actor
to dis is to disparage

explanation.surface: An amateur speaks disparagingly of millions in a cult.
explanation.definitionFit: Mahdism is the Islamic belief in the coming of the Mahdi, a redeemer.

clue.text: Maybe Glaswegian home around capital

indicators.note: home goes around the excellent letters

parts.note: to be in is to be at home
A1 means capital, first-rate, with the 1 read as I

explanation.surface: A Glasgow native lives near the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: Maybe marks Glaswegian as an example: a typical Scottish man's name. The clash with 28 Across puts H first, giving HAIN, Scots for to save, and the final H of CLASH.
explanation.definitionFit: Iain is the Scottish spelling of John, so a Glaswegian might well bear it.

clue.text: For reporter, any editors will be necessary

indicators.note: for a reporter means as heard aloud, so the word stands for the letters it sounds like

parts.note: said quickly, any sounds like the letters N and E
editors, plural, gives two eds

explanation.surface: A journalist says any editor will be needed.
explanation.definitionFit: Needed is required, essential: something you cannot do without.

clue.text: Nearly get rid of can — there's drink in it

indicators.note: nearly means the last letter is cut

parts.note: to demit is to dismiss or give up
can and john are both slang for a toilet

explanation.surface: Almost throwing away a tin with something left in it.
explanation.definitionFit: A demijohn is a large narrow-necked bottle used for wine or home brewing.
